component.name: GaugeDeck
component.summary: Car-style gauges for your PC's temps, fans and load

description.p: GaugeDeck shows your computer's vital signs as a dashboard of car-style dials: CPU temperature and load, GPU temperature and fan, system fans, RAM use and board temperature.
Alerts warn you with a notification, an alarm sound and a flashing gauge when a temperature stays too high or a fan stops spinning.

It is a native GTK 4 app, so it works on current GNOME Wayland desktops where desktop widgets such as Conky no longer display or can freeze the session. Every sensor the computer reports is found and named automatically: processors, graphics cards (including NVIDIA compute cards), drives, motherboard chips and fans. Any of them can be shown as a gauge. Gauges can be restyled with colors, glow, shapes and your own pictures, moved into their own windows, pinned to the dock, or shown as a slim strip. Sensors are only read; nothing on the system is changed.
A fan that stops no longer raises a false alarm on laptops and graphics cards that switch their fan off when cool. The alarm now needs the machine to be warm (fan_stop_temp, 65 by default).
Customize window: colors, shapes, glow and pictures, with ready-made looks. New gauge styles: ring, bar, digital and graph.

Every sensor on the computer is found and named, with a Sensors window to choose which ones to show. Sensors with nothing connected (motherboard chips list many) are marked, kept off and never raise alerts. NVIDIA cards are found with nvidia-smi alone, including headless servers.

Pop any gauge out into its own window, pin it to the dock, or use the compact strip. Pop-outs close with the deck. Sensors are read in the background so the window never freezes, and drawing is cached so the CPU use stays low.

Works with GTK older than 4.10 (Debian 12, MX Linux) and on desktops without a GNOME dock. The installer no longer erases other settings when a title is given, and uninstall removes everything the update added.
Temperature and power gauges for an NVIDIA compute card running next to an AMD or Intel display card, with a temperature alert.
Test alert also flashes a gauge for 10 seconds.
Alerts: notification, alarm sound and flashing gauge for high temperatures, high memory use and stopped fans.
Installer now installs python3-gi-cairo; clearer error if it is missing.
Fan gauges use the machine's own fan names when available.
